name: Karmayoga, the yoga of action (as taught in BhG 2–3)
method_summary: Undertake action with the organs of action, the senses controlled by the mind, without attachment (3.7); do the prescribed action, since action is better than inaction (3.8); act for the sake of sacrifice, free from attachment (3.9); keep one's entitlement to the action and not to its fruit, the fruit not being the motive (2.47); act established in yoga, the same in success and failure (2.48); act, as the knower does, for holding the world together (3.20, 3.25).

warnings.text: One should not be attached to inaction (2.47); outward restraint of the organs of action while dwelling on objects in the mind is hypocrisy (3.6).
Action other than for the sake of sacrifice binds the world (3.9).

signs_of_progress: Casting off good and evil deeds (2.50); freedom from the bondage of action and of birth (2.39, 2.51, 3.9); attaining the highest and perfection (3.19–20).

name: Buddhiyoga, the yoga of understanding (BhG 2.39–53)
method_summary: Hold the understanding 'according to yoga' in acting (2.39): a single, resolute understanding (2.41); take refuge in understanding rather than making the fruit the motive (2.49); be the same in success and failure — equanimity is yoga, and yoga is skill in actions (2.48, 2.50); let the understanding cross the thicket of delusion and stand immovable in samādhi (2.52–53).

warnings.text: Those attached to enjoyment and power, carried away by the flowery speech of the Veda-delighters, do not have resolute understanding in samādhi (2.42–44).
The understandings of the irresolute are many-branched and endless (2.41).

stage: all; culminates in understanding immovable in samādhi (2.53)
signs_of_progress: No effort is lost and even a little protects from great fear (2.40); casting off good and evil deeds (2.50); freedom from the bondage of birth (2.51); nirveda towards what is heard (2.52); attaining yoga (2.53).

name: Restraint and withdrawal of the senses (BhG 2–3)
method_summary: Withdraw the senses from their objects on every side, as a tortoise draws in its limbs (2.58); restraining all of them, sit disciplined, intent on Kṛṣṇa (2.61); move among objects with senses free of passion and aversion and under the self's control (2.64); in karmayoga control the senses by the mind (3.7); against desire, control the senses first (3.41); do not come under the sway of passion and aversion set in each sense (3.34).

equivalents.note: The Gītā's withdrawal of the senses from their objects (tortoise image); the word pratyāhāra is not used in ch. 1–3.

warnings.text: The turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise man who strives (2.60); the mind following the roving senses carries away wisdom like wind a ship (2.67).
Restraining the organs of action while recalling objects in the mind is hypocrisy (3.6); beings follow their nature — what will suppression achieve? (3.33).

stage: all; firmly established in the one of steady wisdom (2.58, 2.68)
signs_of_progress: Wisdom firmly established (2.58, 2.61, 2.68); the relish itself turns away once the highest is seen (2.59); serenity (2.64).

name: Enduring the pairs of opposites (titikṣā)
method_summary: Endure the sense-contacts that give cold and heat, pleasure and pain, which come and go and are impermanent (2.14).
signs_of_progress: The steadfast person whom they do not disturb, the same in pain and pleasure, is fit for immortality (2.15).

name: Performing one's own dharma (svadharma)
method_summary: Look to one's own dharma and do not waver: for a kṣatriya, fight a battle that accords with dharma (2.31); perform one's own dharma even if imperfectly rather than another's well (3.35).

warnings.text: Abandoning one's own dharma incurs sin and disgrace (2.33–36); another's dharma brings fear (3.35).

name: Sacrifice (yajña) as taught in BhG 3.9–16
method_summary: Perform action for the sake of sacrifice, free from attachment (3.9); nourish the gods with sacrifice as they nourish humans (3.11); offer to the gods what they give before enjoying it (3.12); eat what remains of the sacrifice (3.13); keep turning the wheel set in motion by Prajāpati (3.16).

warnings.text: One who enjoys the gods' gifts without offering to them is a thief (3.12); those who cook only for themselves eat sin (3.13); one who does not keep the wheel turning, delighting in the senses, lives in vain (3.16).

signs_of_progress: The highest good through mutual nourishment (3.11); freedom from all faults for eaters of the remainder (3.13).

name: Eating the remainder of the sacrifice
method_summary: The good eat what remains of the sacrifice and are freed from all faults, whereas those who cook for their own sake eat sin (3.13).

warnings.text: Those who cook only for their own sake eat sin (3.13).

name: Renouncing all actions in Kṛṣṇa (BhG 3.30)
method_summary: Renouncing all actions in Kṛṣṇa, with a mind directed to the self, free of expectation and of 'mine', and with the fever gone, act (fight) (3.30); those who follow this teaching constantly, with faith and without carping, are freed from actions (3.31).

warnings.text: Those who carp at this teaching and do not follow it are deluded about all knowledge and lost (3.32).

name: Offering rice-balls and water to the ancestors (piṇḍodaka-kriyā)
method_summary: Mentioned only: Arjuna says that when a family's classes are mixed its ancestors fall, deprived of the rites of offering rice-balls and water (1.42). The chunk gives no procedure.
